findings.summary: Slither triage document itemizes calls-loop as "8 instances" (items 8-15) but an independent re-run of `slither . --exclude-dependencies --json` produces exactly 10 distinct calls-loop results, not 8.
findings.evidence: Independent `slither` JSON output parsed programmatically: calls-loop count = 10. Manually enumerated the 10 call sites from the raw detector text (SweepExecutor.executeSweep baseline read, received-amount read, _executeSwap before/adapter.swap/actualOut reads, _executeActions burn call, _returnRemainders remainder read, PancakeV2Adapter._pairFor/_getReserves/_swap). The document's low-severity section header total ("Low severity (15)") is arithmetically consistent only with calls-loop=10 (10+3 timestamp+2 operator-fee-outlier=15), contradicting its own body text claiming 8 instances.
findings.reproduction: cd packages/contracts && slither . --exclude-dependencies --json /tmp/s.json && python3 -c "import json,collections; d=json.load(open('/tmp/s.json')); print(collections.Counter(r['check'] for r in d['results']['detectors'])['calls-loop'])" # prints 10
findings.failure_scenario: Not exploitable — this is a documentation counting error, not a code defect. The category-level rationale given (all loops bounded by MAX_ACTIONS=50) applies equally to all 10 actual instances, so no unaddressed loop exists. Risk is solely that a future reviewer trusting the itemized list undercounts what was actually triaged.
findings.consequence: None to fund safety. Minor erosion of trust in the Slither triage document's self-reported completeness/precision.
findings.remediation: Update slither-triage.md's calls-loop section to enumerate all 10 actual call sites (or explicitly state the count as 10 and adjust the itemized numbering 8-17), so the itemized list and the section-total header (15) are consistent.

findings.summary: F7-08 through F7-13 is described as covering "six Slither High/Medium findings," but the accompanying table only lists five rows (F7-08 through F7-12); no distinct F7-13 row exists, even though the P3 total (10) in the summary table only reconciles if F7-08..F7-13 is treated as 6 items.
findings.evidence: Table under "F7-08 through F7-13" has exactly 5 rows: arbitrary-send-eth, reentrancy-balance, proxy-storage-collision, amm-spot-oracle-dependency, and "unused-return (×2)" merged into a single row. slither-triage.md separately and correctly triages both unused-return findings as distinct items (findings 5 and 6), so the underlying triage work is complete — only the findings.md summary table's row-to-ID mapping is inconsistent.
findings.reproduction: Read artifacts/security/findings.md lines 135-147 and compare row count (5) against the header's claimed range (F7-08 through F7-13 = 6 IDs) and the P3 summary row's count (10, which requires 6 items in this bucket to sum correctly).
findings.failure_scenario: Not exploitable. Both underlying Slither findings this covers (the two unused-return instances) are individually triaged with sound reasoning in slither-triage.md; only the summary table in findings.md has a labeling/row-count inconsistency.
findings.consequence: None to fund safety. Minor traceability gap between the finding-ID scheme and its own summary table.
findings.remediation: Split the merged "unused-return (×2)" row into two rows (F7-12, F7-13) in findings.md to match the stated ID range and the slither-triage.md itemization.

findings.summary: The witness-binding field table still lists "adapter" (the pre-RA-01 arbitrary-address field name) instead of "adapterKind" (the current closed-enum field), a stale reference left over from before the RA-01 remediation renamed this field.
findings.evidence: Table row: "every swap: tokenIn, amountIn, adapter, minAmountOut, keccak256(routeData), allowFailure" — but SweepPlanLib.sol's SwapAction struct has no field named `adapter`; the actual field is `adapterKind` (SweepPlanLib.AdapterKind). golden-vectors.md's own revision history documents this exact rename.
findings.reproduction: Compare docs/permit2-witness-model.md:26 against packages/contracts/src/libraries/SweepPlanLib.sol's SwapAction struct definition and _hashSwapActions implementation.
findings.failure_scenario: Not exploitable — the contract code and its tests are correct; only this one doc table cell uses stale terminology.
findings.consequence: None to fund safety. Could mildly confuse a future reader cross-referencing this doc against the current struct.
findings.remediation: Update the table cell from "adapter" to "adapterKind" to match the current struct field name.

findings.summary: The audit brief requested review of `docs/fixed-adapter-architecture.md`, but no such file exists in the repository; the closest analogous document is `docs/approval-architecture.md`.
findings.evidence: `ls docs/` shows: approval-architecture.md, architecture.md, audit-preparation.md, implementation-plan.md, permit2-witness-model.md, pricing-and-oracle-model.md, requirements-traceability.md, risk-register.md, security-addendum-review.md, security-model.md, threat-model.md, token-support-model.md, research/ — no fixed-adapter-architecture.md.
findings.failure_scenario: Not exploitable — no code or security implication. Either the brief referenced a planned-but-unwritten doc name, or the actual content lives under a different filename (docs/approval-architecture.md covers closely related material and was reviewed as a substitute).
findings.consequence: None to fund safety. Minor documentation-inventory gap between what the operating brief expects and what exists.
findings.remediation: Either author docs/fixed-adapter-architecture.md (if distinct content was intended beyond what security-model.md §1 and approval-architecture.md already cover) or update whichever checklist names this file to point at the correct existing doc.

findings.summary: The root package.json defines a `format` script (`prettier --check .`) but no `format:check` script; running the literal command `pnpm format:check` (as named in this audit's own instructions and implied by common CI convention) fails with ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC_FIRST_FAIL.
findings.evidence: `pnpm format:check` → "Command \"format:check\" not found. Did you mean \"format:write\"?" package.json scripts are: build, typecheck, lint, format, format:write, test, security:secrets, contracts:build, contracts:test — no format:check.
findings.failure_scenario: Not exploitable. A CI pipeline or reviewer literally invoking `pnpm format:check` (matching this audit brief's naming) would get a spurious failure rather than a formatting result; `pnpm format` is the actual working equivalent and was confirmed clean.
findings.consequence: None to fund safety. Minor script-naming inconsistency that could confuse CI configuration or onboarding.
findings.remediation: Either rename the `format` script to `format:check` (matching the more common Prettier convention alongside `format:write`) or document that `pnpm format` is the check command.

pnpm_audit_vulnerabilities.scope: apps/api hono dependency, out of contract scope
